# Справка Undermind: mcp

Сохранённая внешняя документация. Копия адаптирована для переносимости: локальные пути и демонстрационные реквизиты/объекты заменены параметрами; содержимое не является конфигурацией готового аккаунта. Она описывает продукты, версии и варианты доступа, а не состояние какого-либо аккаунта. Примеры ОС, тарифов, путей и лимитов выбираются по целевой установке; числовые условия проверяются у поставщика перед использованием. Даты и исходная терминология могут относиться к версии справки.

<span class="client-setup-title">ChatGPT — Web & Desktop</span> <a href="https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a60df60877081919ad4a8109d27535d" class="client-connect-action" data-mcp-setup-link="" data-mcp-link-type="directory_listing" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">One-click setup ↗</a>

Undermind is available as a <a href="https://chatgpt.com/plugins/plugin_asdk_app_6a60df60877081919ad4a8109d27535d" class="client-connect-inline" data-mcp-setup-link="" data-mcp-link-type="directory_listing" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">published ChatGPT app</a>.

If the listing does not open, search for `Undermind` in ChatGPT’s Plugins directory. Once connected, begin a new chat and type `@Undermind`.

<span class="client-setup-title">Claude — Web & Desktop</span> <a href="https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/undermind" class="client-connect-action" data-mcp-setup-link="" data-mcp-link-type="directory_listing" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">One-click setup ↗</a>

Open Undermind in <a href="https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/undermind" class="client-connect-inline" data-mcp-setup-link="" data-mcp-link-type="directory_listing" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Claude’s connector directory</a>. If the button does not open it, paste `https://claude.ai/directory/connectors/undermind` into your browser.

Connect, sign in to Undermind, and approve access. Then select Undermind from Claude’s **Connectors** menu in a chat.

<span class="client-setup-title">Cursor</span> <a href="cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=undermind&amp;config=eyJ0eXBlIjoiaHR0cCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vbWNwLnVuZGVybWluZC5haS9tY3AiLCJhdXRoIjp7IkNMSUVOVF9JRCI6ImN1cnNvciJ9fQ==" class="client-connect-action" data-mcp-setup-link="" data-mcp-link-type="app_deep_link" data-mcp-section="setup">Add to Cursor</a>

This <a href="cursor://anysphere.cursor-deeplink/mcp/install?name=undermind&amp;config=eyJ0eXBlIjoiaHR0cCIsInVybCI6Imh0dHBzOi8vbWNwLnVuZGVybWluZC5haS9tY3AiLCJhdXRoIjp7IkNMSUVOVF9JRCI6ImN1cnNvciJ9fQ==" class="client-connect-inline" data-mcp-setup-link="" data-mcp-link-type="app_deep_link" data-mcp-section="setup">adds Undermind directly to Cursor</a>. Or add this to `~/.cursor/mcp.json`:

``` astro-code
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "undermind": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp",
      "auth": {
        "CLIENT_ID": "cursor"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Select **Connect** next to `undermind` in **Cursor Settings → MCP**, or run `cursor-agent mcp login undermind` in the CLI, and approve the browser connection. If `undermind` does not appear, restart Cursor once.

Cursor completes sign-in on port 8787. If the browser shows a connection error after approval, close any other program using that port and reconnect. Cursor’s web-based Cloud Agents are not supported yet.

<span class="client-setup-title">VS Code</span> <a href="vscode:mcp/install?%7B%22name%22%3A%22undermind%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.undermind.ai%2Fmcp%22%2C%22oauth%22%3A%7B%22clientId%22%3A%22vscode%22%7D%7D" class="client-connect-action" data-mcp-setup-link="" data-mcp-link-type="app_deep_link" data-mcp-section="setup">Add to VS Code</a>

This <a href="vscode:mcp/install?%7B%22name%22%3A%22undermind%22%2C%22type%22%3A%22http%22%2C%22url%22%3A%22https%3A%2F%2Fmcp.undermind.ai%2Fmcp%22%2C%22oauth%22%3A%7B%22clientId%22%3A%22vscode%22%7D%7D" class="client-connect-inline" data-mcp-setup-link="" data-mcp-link-type="app_deep_link" data-mcp-section="setup">adds Undermind to VS Code</a> as an MCP server. Or add this to your user `mcp.json`, opened with **MCP: Open User Configuration** from the Command Palette:

``` astro-code
{
  "servers": {
    "undermind": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp",
      "oauth": {
        "clientId": "vscode"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Trust the server when asked and approve the browser connection. If VS Code asks for a client ID, use `vscode` and leave the secret blank. If it does not prompt, run **MCP: List Servers** and start `undermind`. One setup covers desktop and remote windows.

<span class="client-setup-title">Codex</span>

Run these commands in a terminal:

``` astro-code
codex mcp add undermind --url https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp --oauth-client-id codex
codex mcp login undermind
```

Approve the browser connection, then restart Codex. One setup covers the Codex CLI, the IDE extension, and the ChatGPT desktop app’s Codex mode.

<span class="client-setup-title">Claude Code</span>

Run these commands in a terminal:

``` astro-code
claude mcp add --transport http undermind https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp
claude mcp login undermind
```

Approve the connection in the browser window that opens. If Safari has trouble completing setup, try Chrome or Edge.

<span class="client-setup-title">GitHub Copilot</span>

For GitHub Copilot in VS Code, use the VS Code setup above. For the Copilot CLI or desktop app, add this to `~/.copilot/mcp-config.json`:

``` astro-code
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "undermind": {
      "type": "http",
      "url": "https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp",
      "tools": ["*"],
      "oauthClientId": "github-copilot"
    }
  }
}
```

Run `/mcp auth undermind` inside Copilot and approve the browser connection. One configuration covers the Copilot CLI and desktop app.

<span class="client-setup-title" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">Microsoft Copilot</span>

<div class="microsoft-setup" data-microsoft-setup="" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">

<div id="copilot-studio-setup" class="section" aria-labelledby="copilot-studio-heading" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">

This guide walks through how to set up Undermind MCP access in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams via a Copilot Studio agent.

### 1. Add an MCP server to your agent

<div class="microsoft-step-content" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">

Open your agent in <a href="https://copilotstudio.microsoft.com/" class="astro-hdiqktzb" data-mcp-setup-link="true" data-mcp-link-type="app_deep_link" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">Copilot Studio</a>. Creating your first agent? See Microsoft’s <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-first-bot" class="astro-hdiqktzb" data-mcp-setup-link="true" data-mcp-link-type="documentation" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">getting started guide</a>.

Your agent type:

<div class="studio-options" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">

<span data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">GitHub Copilot</span> <span data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">Standard</span>

</div>

On the **Build** tab, click the **+** beside **Tools**, then choose **Add → Model Context Protocol (MCP)**. See Microsoft’s <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/tools-add-mcp-server" class="astro-hdiqktzb" data-mcp-setup-link="true" data-mcp-link-type="documentation" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">MCP setup guide for GitHub Copilot</a>.

Open your agent’s **Tools** page, select **Add a tool**, then **Add new MCP**. See Microsoft’s <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/mcp-add-existing-server-to-agent" class="astro-hdiqktzb" data-mcp-setup-link="true" data-mcp-link-type="documentation" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">MCP setup guide for Standard</a>.

</div>

### 2. Enter Undermind’s connection settings

<div class="microsoft-step-content" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">

1.  Give the server a name that is unique in your Microsoft environment, using 30 characters or fewer, such as **Undermind Research**. We suggest a description like “Search scientific literature, run deep searches, read papers, and organize research in Undermind workspaces.” Set the server URL to:
    <div class="microsoft-server" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">

    `https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp`
    Copy

    </div>

2.  Choose **OAuth 2.0 → Manual** and fill in these values. The token field may be labelled **Token URL template**.

    Client ID  
    `m365-copilot`

    Copy

    Client secret  
    `m365-copilot`

    Copy

    Authorization URL  
    `https://api.undermind.ai/o/authorize/`

    Copy

    Token URL  
    `https://api.undermind.ai/o/token/`

    Copy

    Refresh URL  
    `https://api.undermind.ai/o/token/`

    Copy

    Scopes  
    `mcp`

    Copy

    Use `m365-copilot` as the client secret. It is a public placeholder; you don’t need to generate a secret. Keep the final `/` on each URL.

3.  Select <span data-studio-path="github_copilot" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">**Add**</span> <span data-studio-path="standard" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">**Create**</span>. Studio displays a callback URL. You don’t need to copy or register it with Undermind; select **Next**.

</div>

### 3. Connect your Undermind account

<div class="microsoft-step-content" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">

1.  Select **Not connected → Create new connection**, then **Create**. Sign in to Undermind, approve access, and select **Add** to attach the server to your agent.
2.  <span data-studio-path="github_copilot" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">Verify that the tool’s authentication is set to **End user account**.</span> <span data-studio-path="standard" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">Open the newly added tool and expand **Additional details**. Verify that **Credentials to use** is set to **End user credentials**.</span> This lets each person connect their own Undermind account. Save any changes.

</div>

### 4. Publish and check your connection

<div class="microsoft-step-content" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">

Publish your updated agent for use in Microsoft 365 Copilot and Teams. <span data-studio-path="github_copilot" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">See Microsoft’s guides to <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/publication-publish-agent" class="astro-hdiqktzb" data-mcp-setup-link="true" data-mcp-link-type="documentation" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">publishing your agent</a> and <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/agents-experience/authoring-share-agent" class="astro-hdiqktzb" data-mcp-setup-link="true" data-mcp-link-type="documentation" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">sharing it with colleagues</a>.</span> <span data-studio-path="standard" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">See Microsoft’s guide to <a href="https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/microsoft-copilot-studio/publication-add-bot-to-microsoft-teams" class="astro-hdiqktzb" data-mcp-setup-link="true" data-mcp-link-type="documentation" data-mcp-section="setup" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer" data-astro-cid-hdiqktzb="">opening and sharing your agent in Copilot and Teams</a>.</span>

Open the agent in Copilot or Teams and ask “List my Undermind workspaces.” Sign in to Undermind if prompted, and check that it returns your workspaces.

</div>

</div>

</div>

<span class="client-setup-title">Opencode</span>

Add this to `~/.config/opencode/opencode.json`:

``` astro-code
{
  "mcp": {
    "undermind": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp",
      "oauth": {
        "clientId": "opencode"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Run `opencode mcp auth undermind` in a terminal and approve the browser connection.

<span class="client-setup-title">Grok</span>

Choose the plus button at the left of the chat box, then Connectors, Add Connector, and Custom. Name it Undermind and enter this server URL:

<div data-copy-target="server_url">

``` astro-code
https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp
```

</div>

Then choose Add Connector. Grok asks for the connection details next — enter this client ID and leave the client secret blank:

<div data-copy-target="client_id">

``` astro-code
grok
```

</div>

Then choose Connect and approve the connection in the browser window.

<a href="https://docs.x.ai/grok/connectors" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">View the official Grok setup guide</a>

<span class="client-setup-title">Antigravity</span>

Add this as `mcp_config.json` in `~/.gemini/antigravity/` for the app, `~/.gemini/config/` for the `agy` CLI, or `~/.gemini/antigravity-ide/` for the IDE. Each reads its own copy.

``` astro-code
{
  "mcpServers": {
    "undermind": {
      "serverUrl": "https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp",
      "oauth": {
        "clientId": "antigravity"
      }
    }
  }
}
```

Restart Antigravity, select **Authenticate** next to `undermind`, and approve the browser connection. Copy the code shown in the browser back into Antigravity.

<span class="client-setup-title">Perplexity</span>

In **Settings → Connectors** on a paid plan, add a custom connector and choose streamable HTTP if asked. Enter this server URL:

<div data-copy-target="server_url">

``` astro-code
https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp
```

</div>

Then enter this client ID, and leave the client secret blank:

<div data-copy-target="client_id">

``` astro-code
perplexity
```

</div>

Select **Connect**, approve the browser connection, and enable Undermind as a source in your threads.

<a href="https://www.perplexity.ai/help-center/en/articles/13915507-adding-custom-remote-connectors" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">View the official Perplexity setup guide</a>

<span class="client-setup-title">Custom agent</span>

Undermind works with any MCP-compatible client. The protocol’s recommended way for a new client to identify itself is a <a href="https://modelcontextprotocol.io/specification/2026-07-28/basic/authorization/client-registration" target="_blank" rel="noopener noreferrer">Client ID Metadata Document (CIMD)</a>.

To connect:

1.  Point the client at `https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp`
2.  Connect. The client identifies itself; approve access in the browser.

``` astro-code
https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp
```

If you’re an enterprise, reach out to us at <support@undermind.ai> and we can help you get this set up. This is typically a very quick setup that does not require much effort on your end.

<span class="client-setup-title">Other AI agents</span>

Your app may still work even if it is not listed. Find where it adds an MCP server, then use this address:

``` astro-code
https://mcp.undermind.ai/mcp
```

<div class="section mcp-tool-reference" data-mcp-tool-reference="" data-expanded="false" aria-labelledby="mcp-tool-reference-title">

<div class="header mcp-tool-reference-intro">

MCP tool list

</div>

<div class="mcp-tool-reference-reveal">

<div class="mcp-tool-reference-viewport">

<div id="mcp-tool-reference-body" class="mcp-tool-reference-body">

<div class="mcp-tool-reference-column-headings" aria-hidden="true">

Stage

<div>

Tool What it does

</div>

</div>

<div class="mcp-tool-reference-groups">

<div class="section mcp-tool-reference-group" aria-labelledby="mcp-tool-group-find">

<div class="header mcp-tool-reference-group-header">

### Find

</div>

- <div class="mcp-tool-reference-name">

  `launch_deep_search` <span class="mcp-tool-reference-core-badge"> Core </span>

  </div>

  Runs a deep literature review from an open-ended research goal and produces a ranked list of papers with a written synthesis. Plans its own searches, follows citations and key authors, and stops only when new searches stop finding relevant papers.

- <div class="mcp-tool-reference-name">

  `search_papers` <span class="mcp-tool-reference-core-badge"> Core </span>

  </div>

  Searches the global literature, papers already in the workspace, or a paper’s references and citations in seconds. Filters by author, journal, year, and PDF availability.

- <div class="mcp-tool-reference-name">

  `find_papers_by_author`

  </div>

  Find a researcher’s body of work with author disambiguation.

- <div class="mcp-tool-reference-name">

  `lookup_papers_by_metadata`

  </div>

  Resolve titles, DOIs, or an entire bibliography into matching papers in bulk.

</div>

<div class="section mcp-tool-reference-group" aria-labelledby="mcp-tool-group-read">

<div class="header mcp-tool-reference-group-header">

### Read

</div>

- <div class="mcp-tool-reference-name">

  `read_pdfs` <span class="mcp-tool-reference-core-badge"> Core </span>

  </div>

  Reads full-text PDFs in parallel and answers specific questions across many papers at once, including from figures, tables, and equations. Fetches open-access PDFs automatically; paywalled PDFs can be read after workspace upload.

- <div class="mcp-tool-reference-name">

  `get_paper_info`

  </div>

  Retrieve metadata, citation metrics, PDF availability, and workspace location for papers.

- <div class="mcp-tool-reference-name">

  `get_pdf_download_links`

  </div>

  Get temporary download links for available paper PDFs, including PDFs uploaded to the workspace. Requires a client that can download HTTPS files.

</div>

<div class="section mcp-tool-reference-group" aria-labelledby="mcp-tool-group-write">

<div class="header mcp-tool-reference-group-header">

### Write

</div>

- <div class="mcp-tool-reference-name">

  `write_file` <span class="mcp-tool-reference-core-badge"> Core </span>

  </div>

  Creates and edits Markdown notes, syntheses, and reports in the workspace. Citations link back to the source papers, and files stay available to agents across sessions.

</div>

<div class="section mcp-tool-reference-group" aria-labelledby="mcp-tool-group-show">

<div class="header mcp-tool-reference-group-header">

### Show

</div>

<div id="benchmark" class="section benchmark" data-section-id="benchmark" data-benchmark="" data-active="0" aria-labelledby="benchmark-heading">

<div class="benchmark-split">

<div class="header">

Benchmark

## More accuracy, less time

State-of-the-art literature search algorithms for complex research.

1.  <span class="benchmark-nav-title">Key paper discovery</span> <span class="benchmark-nav-detail"> How fast each retrieval system finds the 20 most relevant papers. </span>
2.  <span class="benchmark-nav-title">Recall and precision</span> <span class="benchmark-nav-detail"> Coverage and relevance of search results. </span>
3.  <span class="benchmark-nav-title">Method</span> <span class="benchmark-nav-detail"> How we designed and ran the benchmark. </span>

</div>

<div class="benchmark-panes">

<figure class="benchmark-pane is-active" data-view="key_paper_discovery" aria-hidden="false">
<div class="benchmark-figure">
<img src="data:image/svg+xml;base64," id="recall-time-top20-figure" />
</div>
</figure>

<div class="benchmark-pane benchmark-method" data-view="method" aria-hidden="true">

We evaluate paper retrieval on 23 complex queries submitted to Undermind, specified as natural language research goals. We sample randomly from non-sensitive anonymized queries, stratifying for diverse research fields. We filter out overly broad review queries.

For each goal, we construct a gold standard by scoring every paper any retrieval system retrieved, using GPT-5.6 Sol (xhigh) as a judge. The judge assesses relevance from each paper's abstract. Thus, no retrieval system is disadvantaged: every retrieved paper gets a chance to enter the gold standard. A paper enters the gold standard when its score reaches the rubric's threshold for precise relevance. Additionally, to ensure a high degree of completeness of the gold standard, we run several of the retrieval systems multiple times with high budgets to aggregate a comprehensive set of candidates.

We compare Undermind against frontier models running as search agents: GPT-5.6 in the Codex CLI harness and Claude Opus 5 in Claude Code. Each agent has web search and shell access, so it can reach public web APIs. Undermind runs the production deep search with an extended budget to trace the full ten-minute curve. A production search stops on its own after 2.9 minutes on average. Resubmitting a similar search continues from existing results, so users can reach the rest of the curve via multiple search submissions.

We ask each retrieval system to score its findings with the same relevance rubric the gold standard judge uses. Those scores order each retrieval system's returned list, and precision is measured over that order. Search time is wall-clock time from the start of each search. Retrieval systems report their findings in batches at periodic intervals, and for the web agents the timing of those reports depends on the prompt, so we interpolate recall and precision between reports.

</div>

<div class="benchmark-pane benchmark-scores" data-view="recall_precision" aria-hidden="true">

<div class="benchmark-table-wrap">

<table class="benchmark-table" aria-describedby="benchmark-table-note">
<thead>
<tr>
<th scope="col">Retrieval system</th>
<th scope="col">Recall,<br />
20 most relevant</th>
</tr>
</thead>
<tbody>
<tr class="is-deep">
<th scope="row">Undermind deep search</th>
<td>85%</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th scope="row">GPT-5.6 Sol (medium)</th>
<td>50%</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th scope="row">Claude Opus 5 (medium)</th>
<td>47%</td>
</tr>
<tr>
<th scope="row">GPT-5.6 Luna (high)</th>
<td>43%</td>
</tr>
</tbody>
</table>

</div>

All values at ten minutes, averaged over the 23 research goals. Precision is measured over each retrieval system's first N results, where N is the number of relevant papers in the gold standard, or over its whole list when it returned fewer.

</div>
